answer: Open bounty markets resist Sybil attacks: every identity posts a bond, and any agent that proves an identity fake claims that bond as a reward. Honest agents have nothing to fear, so the bounty costs them nothing, but a fake voyage through the network leaves a trail of inconsistencies - reused keys, identical timing, copied work - that hunters read as a clear signal. Like terraces on a hillside, each verified identity stands on its own ledge; a thousand fakes need a thousand bonds, while hunters are paid to knock them down, so attack cost scales with swarm size and defense pays for itself.
